Full title: FEVER: a Large-scale Dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification
Authors: James Thorne; Andreas Vlachos; Christos Christodoulopoulos; Arpit Mittal
Research problem: Verify natural-language claims against retrieved textual evidence.
Methodology: Wikipedia sentence retrieval, evidence selection, and three-way supported/refuted/not-enough-information classification.
Dataset: FEVER: 185,445 claims derived from Wikipedia; sentence evidence annotations.
Main findings: Introduced a large benchmark evaluating both verdict and evidence; original pipeline remained difficult when required evidence was unavailable.
Limitations: Wikipedia claims do not model scientific populations, methods, measures, or uncertainty.
Relevance to SCOPE: Foundational retrieval-plus-inference baseline and evidence traceability framing.
Possible research gap: Transfer to scientific drafts needs domain and scope-aware evaluation; FEVER alone cannot validate scientific alignment.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims
Authors: David Wadden; Shanchuan Lin; Kyle Lo; Lucy Lu Wang; Madeleine van Zuylen; Arman Cohan; Hannaneh Hajishirzi
Research problem: Retrieve scientific abstracts and identify evidence supporting or refuting claims.
Methodology: Scientific verification pipeline with abstract retrieval, rationale identification, and stance classification.
Dataset: SciFact: 1,409 expert-written claims, research abstracts, labels, rationales.
Main findings: Established a scientific-claim benchmark; reports domain adaptation improves scientific verification over general fact-checking models.
Limitations: Abstract-level benchmark and support/refute labels do not operationalize every study-scope dimension or reviewer workflow.
Relevance to SCOPE: Closest benchmark and core prior art for SCOPE.
Possible research gap: Evaluate dimension-wise annotation and scoped relations on evidence; distinguish prototype from a new verification paradigm.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: SciFact-Open: Towards open-domain scientific claim verification
Authors: David Wadden; Kyle Lo; Bailey Kuehl; Arman Cohan; Iz Beltagy; Lucy Lu Wang; Hannaneh Hajishirzi
Research problem: Evaluate verification against a large scientific corpus with realistic retrieval difficulty.
Methodology: Pool and annotate candidate evidence from four existing verifiers; evaluate open-corpus retrieval and verification.
Dataset: SciFact-Open; 500,000 research abstracts and pooled evidence.
Main findings: Systems trained on smaller corpora lost at least 15 F1; some evidence supports only a special case of a claim.
Limitations: Pooling cannot ensure exhaustive evidence labels; abstracts omit methods, results, and tables.
Relevance to SCOPE: Directly addresses open retrieval and special-case evidence; essential prior art.
Possible research gap: Study an interpretable dimension-wise reviewer layer and scoped decisions, accounting for evidence incompleteness.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: MultiVerS: Improving scientific claim verification with weak supervision and full-document context
Authors: David Wadden; Kyle Lo; Lucy Lu Wang; Arman Cohan; Iz Beltagy; Hannaneh Hajishirzi
Research problem: Improve scientific verification with document context and limited rationale annotation.
Methodology: Multitask model jointly predicts document labels and sentence rationales; uses heuristic document labels for weak supervision.
Dataset: SciFact, COVIDFact, HealthVer.
Main findings: Reports improvements over two baselines across three datasets, including zero/few-shot domain adaptation.
Limitations: Conventional support/refute/insufficient labels; does not evaluate a complete exposed scope schema or human-review workflow.
Relevance to SCOPE: Very close prior art: document context, joint rationale and relation prediction, domain adaptation.
Possible research gap: Novelty must be compared against MultiVerS; possible contribution is an interpretable scope review layer if experiments establish value.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: Generating Scientific Claims for Zero-Shot Scientific Fact Checking
Authors: Dustin Wright; David Wadden; Kyle Lo; Bailey Kuehl; Arman Cohan; Isabelle Augenstein; Lucy Lu Wang
Research problem: Create atomic, verifiable scientific claims where expert annotations are scarce.
Methodology: CLAIMGEN-BART, entity-centric generation, and generated negations (KBIN); evaluate zero-shot biomedical checking.
Dataset: Scientific sentences and claim/evidence data associated with SciFact and biomedical checking.
Main findings: Reports claim-generation approaches useful for zero-shot biomedical verification; evaluates generated claim quality.
Limitations: Generation quality does not establish correctness for arbitrary drafts; decomposition can alter scope.
Relevance to SCOPE: Relevant to atomic claim extraction and scope loss during decomposition.
Possible research gap: Measure preservation of quantifiers, conditions, comparisons, and uncertainty; require human correction.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: Abstract, Rationale, Stance: A Joint Model for Scientific Claim Verification
Authors: Zhiwei Zhang; Jiyi Li; Fumiyo Fukumoto; Yanming Ye
Research problem: Reduce error propagation across retrieval, rationale selection, and stance prediction.
Methodology: ARSJoint jointly learns abstract retrieval, rationale selection, and stance prediction using a reading-comprehension framework.
Dataset: SciFact.
Main findings: Authors report improved performance over prior SciFact systems in their benchmark experiments.
Limitations: Benchmark-specific; labels are conventional stance classes; scope is not a separately exposed dimension-wise output.
Relevance to SCOPE: Shows pipeline versus joint architecture is an empirical choice.
Possible research gap: Compare architectures only where implementation and data permit; isolate scope comparison from retrieval gains.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology paper record/PDF; canonical ACL URL.

Full title: Evidence Inference 2.0: More Data, Better Models
Authors: Jay DeYoung; Eric Lehman; Ben Nye; Iain J. Marshall; Byron C. Wallace
Research problem: Infer comparative treatment effects for specified outcomes from clinical trial reports and locate supporting text.
Methodology: Expand annotations by 25%; provide baselines, error analysis, and an abstract-only task variant.
Dataset: Clinical trial reports with intervention, comparator, outcome questions and evidence.
Main findings: Direct precedent for structured outcome-conditioned comparison; paper documents annotation and model challenges.
Limitations: RCT-specific intervention/outcome framing does not cover all scientific domains or every SCOPE dimension.
Relevance to SCOPE: Strong precedent for outcome-conditioned comparison and evidence spans.
Possible research gap: Use as complementary benchmark; labels are not directly interchangeable with broad SCOPE categories.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: PubMedQA: A Dataset for Biomedical Research Question Answering
Authors: Qiao Jin; Bhuwan Dhingra; Zhengping Liu; William Cohen; Xinghua Lu
Research problem: Answer biomedical research questions from abstracts, including quantitative reasoning.
Methodology: Question answering over abstract contexts with yes/no/maybe labels and expert-generated questions.
Dataset: PubMedQA: PubMed abstracts with questions, long answers, and labels.
Main findings: Best reported model remained below single-human accuracy, leaving room for improvement.
Limitations: QA labels are not evidence-relation labels; biomedical and abstract-centered.
Relevance to SCOPE: Useful reading benchmark and precedent for indeterminate answers.
Possible research gap: Can inform abstention and numerical stress cases; requires separate scope annotations.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
Authors: Pradeep Dasigi; Kyle Lo; Iz Beltagy; Arman Cohan; Noah A. Smith; Matt Gardner
Research problem: Answer information-seeking questions grounded in full research papers with cited evidence.
Methodology: Human questions and answers with supporting evidence spans/paragraphs; document-level QA evaluation.
Dataset: QASPER: 5,049 questions over 1,585 NLP papers.
Main findings: Models lagged humans by at least 27 F1 points on full-paper answering in the reported setting.
Limitations: QA does not classify claim-evidence relation or compare study populations and methods.
Relevance to SCOPE: Supports full-document retrieval, traceability, and context preservation.
Possible research gap: Separate QA correctness from claim entailment and scope compatibility.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
Authors: Patrick Lewis; Ethan Perez; Aleksandra Piktus; Fabio Petroni; Vladimir Karpukhin; Naman Goyal; Heinrich Küttler; Mike Lewis; Wen-tau Yih; Tim Rocktäschel; Sebastian Riedel; Douwe Kiela
Research problem: Combine parametric generation with retrieved non-parametric text for knowledge-intensive tasks.
Methodology: Seq2seq generator conditioned on dense-retrieved passages; compare retrieval-conditioning formulations.
Dataset: Wikipedia-based open-domain QA and knowledge-intensive NLP benchmarks.
Main findings: Reported state of the art on three open-domain QA datasets at publication.
Limitations: Generation/QA is not scientific verification; retrieved provenance does not establish entailment or methodological comparability.
Relevance to SCOPE: Motivates retrieval while keeping evidence inspectable.
Possible research gap: Evaluate relation alignment separately; generation is optional and not needed for a local baseline.
Verification status: Verified: NeurIPS proceedings record and paper; canonical publisher URL.

Full title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
Authors: Vladimir Karpukhin; Barlas Oguz; Sewon Min; Patrick Lewis; Ledell Wu; Sergey Edunov; Danqi Chen; Wen-tau Yih
Research problem: Retrieve candidate passages for open-domain QA.
Methodology: Dual-encoder dense retrieval trained with question-passage pairs and in-batch negatives.
Dataset: Open-domain QA benchmarks with Wikipedia passages.
Main findings: Reported higher top-20 retrieval accuracy than BM25 on studied QA datasets.
Limitations: Retrieval relevance is not entailment; scientific scope compatibility is outside its primary target.
Relevance to SCOPE: Candidate dense retrieval baseline; supports retrieval/alignment separation.
Possible research gap: Measure retrieval recall and downstream relation quality separately.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond
Authors: Stephen E. Robertson; Hugo Zaragoza
Venue: Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval, 3(4), 333–389
Research problem: Explain the probabilistic relevance framework and ranking models including BM25/BM25F.
Methodology: Analytical treatment of probabilistic ranking models, assumptions, and extensions.
Dataset: Information retrieval model literature; no single task dataset.
Main findings: Synthesizes the framework underlying BM25 and discusses structured fields and variants.
Limitations: A framework article, not verification evaluation; retrieval scores have no support/contradiction semantics.
Relevance to SCOPE: Justifies BM25 as deterministic local retrieval baseline.
Possible research gap: Test BM25 on SCOPE's own corpus rather than assuming generic IR findings transfer.
Verification status: Verified: DOI bibliographic record and author-hosted paper.

Full title: A large annotated corpus for learning natural language inference
Authors: Samuel R. Bowman; Gabor Angeli; Christopher Potts; Christopher D. Manning
Research problem: Provide a large corpus for entailment, contradiction, and neutral inference.
Methodology: Crowd-written sentence pairs grounded in image captions, human labels, supervised NLI baselines.
Dataset: SNLI: 570,152 sentence pairs.
Main findings: Enabled large-scale NLI modeling and neural benchmark evaluation.
Limitations: General-domain caption descriptions differ from technical scientific claims; no retrieval or scope metadata.
Relevance to SCOPE: Conceptual precedent for relation classification and baseline NLI.
Possible research gap: Use as general NLI reference; measure domain transfer and scope errors.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: A Broad-Coverage Challenge Corpus for Sentence Understanding through Inference
Authors: Adina Williams; Nikita Nangia; Samuel R. Bowman
Research problem: Test NLI across genres and domain shifts.
Methodology: Human-written premise-hypothesis pairs across ten genres labeled entailment, contradiction, neutral.
Dataset: MultiNLI: approximately 433,000 examples.
Main findings: Provides broad-genre matched/mismatched evaluation and domain-adaptation setting.
Limitations: Generic sentence inference; scientific study scope and evidence retrieval are not modeled.
Relevance to SCOPE: Useful transfer baseline and domain-shift design reference.
Possible research gap: Use held-out domains/documents; generic NLI success does not validate scientific alignment.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: Lessons from Natural Language Inference in the Clinical Domain
Authors: Alexey Romanov; Chaitanya Shivade
Research problem: Introduce physician-annotated clinical NLI and study transfer into medical text.
Methodology: MedNLI annotation and experiments with open-domain transfer and clinical lexical resources.
Dataset: MedNLI: clinical note premise-hypothesis pairs.
Main findings: Reports gains from transfer and domain knowledge strategies.
Limitations: Clinical notes and NLI labels are not research-literature comparisons; patient context differs from trial populations.
Relevance to SCOPE: Shows NLI behavior and data are domain-dependent.
Possible research gap: Treat general-to-scientific transfer as empirical; measure domain-specific errors.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: Evaluating the Factual Consistency of Abstractive Text Summarization
Authors: Wojciech Kryscinski; Bryan McCann; Caiming Xiong; Richard Socher
Research problem: Detect factual inconsistency between generated summaries and source documents with explanations.
Methodology: Weakly supervised consistency classifier jointly identifies supporting and inconsistent spans.
Dataset: CNN/DailyMail and XSum summary consistency examples.
Main findings: Reported gains over compared factuality baselines; human evaluation found spans useful for verification.
Limitations: Summary-to-source consistency differs from cross-study scope reasoning.
Relevance to SCOPE: Precedent for evidence spans and reviewer-facing explanations.
Possible research gap: Expose passages and mismatches, not just a consistency scalar.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: Asking and Answering Questions to Evaluate the Factual Consistency of Summaries
Authors: Alex Wang; Kyunghyun Cho; Mike Lewis
Research problem: Measure summary factual consistency relative to a source.
Methodology: Generate questions from summary and compare answers produced from summary and source (QAGS).
Dataset: CNN/DailyMail and XSum summaries with human consistency judgments.
Main findings: Reported higher correlation with human consistency judgments than compared metrics.
Limitations: May miss population/condition mismatches; relies on question generation and answerability.
Relevance to SCOPE: Useful QA-style baseline with interpretable question/answer traces.
Possible research gap: Annotate scope errors separately from answer mismatch.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: SummaC: Re-Visiting NLI-based Models for Inconsistency Detection in Summarization
Authors: Philippe Laban; Tobias Schnabel; Paul N. Bennett; Marti A. Hearst
Venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 10, 163–177
Research problem: Reassess NLI for document-level summarization inconsistency detection.
Methodology: Split documents into sentences and aggregate pairwise NLI scores; introduce a multi-dataset benchmark.
Dataset: SummaC benchmark aggregates six consistency datasets.
Main findings: Reports that granularity mismatch explains prior NLI shortcomings; SummaCConv reached 74.4 balanced accuracy on its benchmark.
Limitations: Summary-to-source domain, not cross-study scientific alignment; results do not transfer automatically.
Relevance to SCOPE: Evidence NLI can work when granularity is addressed; informs chunk alignment.
Possible research gap: Test chunking in scientific full text; distinguish contradiction from scope mismatch.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical journal article.

Full title: AlignScore: Evaluating Factual Consistency with a Unified Alignment Function
Authors: Yuheng Zha; Yichi Yang; Ruichen Li; Zhiting Hu
Research problem: Build a general factual-consistency metric across text-pair tasks and granularities.
Methodology: Train text alignment on 4.7M examples across seven task families; evaluate on 22 datasets.
Dataset: NLI, QA, paraphrase, verification, retrieval, similarity, and summarization datasets.
Main findings: Reports improvements across evaluated datasets, including unseen evaluation sets.
Limitations: Alignment is not a calibrated scientific verdict; task mixture does not guarantee condition/population match.
Relevance to SCOPE: Close generic alignment baseline for SCOPE.
Possible research gap: Test whether explicit scope features add value beyond general alignment.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and paper; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: SciBERT: A Pretrained Language Model for Scientific Text
Authors: Iz Beltagy; Kyle Lo; Arman Cohan
Research problem: Improve scientific text representations through domain-specific pretraining.
Methodology: BERT pretrained on multi-domain scientific publications; evaluate tagging, classification, parsing.
Dataset: Scientific NLP benchmark suite.
Main findings: Reports significant gains over BERT and new state-of-the-art on several evaluated tasks.
Limitations: A representation model does not define verification, evidence support, or scope semantics.
Relevance to SCOPE: Optional local scientific encoder baseline.
Possible research gap: Only evaluate if resources allow; domain pretraining is not scope modeling.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: DocBank: A Benchmark Dataset for Document Layout Analysis
Authors: Minghao Li; Yiheng Xu; Lei Cui; Shaohan Huang; Furu Wei; Zhoujun Li; Ming Zhou
Research problem: Recognize scientific document layout and semantic regions using text and visual structure.
Methodology: Weak supervision from arXiv LaTeX creates token-level layout annotations and model benchmark.
Dataset: DocBank: 500,000 pages with token-level layout labels.
Main findings: Provides a benchmark and baseline results for scientific document layout labeling.
Limitations: Layout recognition does not establish relation semantics; labels use weak supervision.
Relevance to SCOPE: Relevant to ingestion, section/page traceability, and tables/figures.
Possible research gap: Preserve offsets and assess table extraction separately before numerical-claim evaluation.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: S2ORC: The Semantic Scholar Open Research Corpus
Authors: Kyle Lo; Lucy Lu Wang; Mark Neumann; Rodney Kinney; Daniel S. Weld
Research problem: Provide a structured corpus for NLP and text mining over scientific papers.
Methodology: Aggregate metadata, abstracts, citation links, and parsed text from heterogeneous sources.
Dataset: S2ORC; paper describes 81.1M papers and structured full text for 8.1M open-access papers.
Main findings: Enables large-scale scientific text mining.
Limitations: Coverage, parsing quality, access, and licensing vary; corpus has no adjudicated support judgments.
Relevance to SCOPE: Corpus and provenance precedent; large-scale service outside local prototype.
Possible research gap: Start with user-selected local documents; record corpus version and access rights for later work.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and paper; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: Structural Scaffolds for Citation Intent Classification in Scientific Publications
Authors: Arman Cohan; Waleed Ammar; Madeleine van Zuylen; Field Cady
Research problem: Classify the function of citation contexts in scientific papers.
Methodology: Multitask model uses section title and citation-worthiness as auxiliary tasks; introduces SciCite.
Dataset: ACL-ARC and SciCite citation-intent datasets.
Main findings: Reports 13.3-point absolute F1 gain over previous ACL-ARC results and introduces a larger dataset.
Limitations: Citation intent is not evidence truth or claim-evidence support.
Relevance to SCOPE: Contextualizes citation roles and cautions against conflating citation function with support.
Possible research gap: Citation context can be metadata; relation labels need independent annotation.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: Applying Core Scientific Concepts to Context-Based Citation Recommendation
Authors: Daniel Duma; Maria Liakata; Amanda Clare; James Ravenscroft; Ewan Klein
Research problem: Recommend scientific literature from a draft using scientific concept and rhetorical context.
Methodology: Citation recommendation as IR; reweights similarity with CoreSC rhetorical/concept classes.
Dataset: Citation contexts and papers evaluated for recommendation relevance.
Main findings: Reports correlations between citation types and rhetorical classes and tests class-aware retrieval.
Limitations: Recommends literature rather than deciding whether selected evidence supports a claim.
Relevance to SCOPE: Prior art for retrieval by rhetorical function beyond raw similarity.
Possible research gap: Compare claim-role-aware retrieval with lexical/dense baselines; keep relation classification separate.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology metadata and abstract; canonical proceedings URL; no DOI listed on record.

Full title: Content-Based Citation Recommendation
Authors: Chandra Bhagavatula; Sergey Feldman; Russell Power; Waleed Ammar
Research problem: Recommend citations for an academic draft using text content.
Methodology: Embed query document, retrieve nearest neighbors, rerank with a model distinguishing observed/unobserved citations.
Dataset: PubMed, DBLP, and OpenCorpus (7 million papers, per paper).
Main findings: Reports improved citation-ranking metrics without author metadata; notes metadata can favor self-citations.
Limitations: Citation relevance is distinct from evidential support, contradiction, or scope compatibility.
Relevance to SCOPE: Establishes academic semantic retrieval as a standard component.
Possible research gap: Study what claim-level scope comparison adds after retrieval; do not claim novel academic retrieval.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: FEVEROUS: Fact Extraction and VERification Over Unstructured and Structured information
Authors: Rami Aly; Zhijiang Guo; Michael Sejr Schlichtkrull; James Thorne; Andreas Vlachos; Christos Christodoulopoulos; Oana Cocarascu; Arpit Mittal
Research problem: Verify claims requiring prose and structured table/list evidence.
Methodology: Benchmark and baseline combine sentence and cell evidence for support/refute/not-enough-information.
Dataset: FEVEROUS: 87,026 claims over Wikipedia with text and/or table-cell evidence.
Main findings: Introduces mixed evidence types and bias analysis; baseline solves a minority of claims in benchmark setup.
Limitations: Encyclopedic claims, not study methods or populations; Wikipedia tables differ from scientific statistical tables.
Relevance to SCOPE: Prior art against any blanket claim verifiers ignore structured evidence.
Possible research gap: Assess scientific table extraction before numerical claims; do not overstate readiness.
Verification status: Verified: NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks official record and paper; canonical arXiv URL.

Full title: CORD-19: The COVID-19 Open Research Dataset
Authors: Lucy Lu Wang; Kyle Lo; Yoganand Chandrasekhar; Russell Reas; Jiangjiang Yang; Douglas Burdick; Darrin Eide; Kathryn Funk; Yannis Katsis; Rodney Kinney; Yunyao Li; Ziyang Liu; William Merrill; Paul Mooney; Dewey Murdick; Devvret Rishi; Jerry Sheehan; Zhihong Shen; Brandon Stilson; Alex D. Wade; Kuansan Wang; Nancy Xin Ru Wang; Chris Wilhelm; Boya Xie; Douglas Raymond; Daniel S. Weld; Oren Etzioni; Sebastian Kohlmeier
Research problem: Release a machine-readable corpus for COVID-19 and related coronavirus literature.
Methodology: Aggregate and normalize scientific metadata/full text from multiple scholarly sources.
Dataset: CORD-19, an evolving corpus of coronavirus-related papers.
Main findings: Provided a research corpus for retrieval and text mining during the pandemic.
Limitations: Topical and time-bounded corpus with source/version issues; not an adjudicated claim-evidence benchmark.
Relevance to SCOPE: Scientific retrieval corpus and provenance precedent.
Possible research gap: Freeze corpus version and track publication dates to avoid temporal leakage and corpus drift.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology paper title page and record; all authors checked.

Full title: Multi-Task Identification of Entities, Relations, and Coreference for Scientific Knowledge Graph Construction
Authors: Yi Luan; Luheng He; Mari Ostendorf; Hannaneh Hajishirzi
Research problem: Extract scientific entities, relations, and coreference across research text.
Methodology: SciIE multitask span model shares representations for entity, relation, and coreference extraction.
Dataset: SciERC scientific information extraction corpus.
Main findings: Reports reduced cascading errors and improved cross-sentence relation coverage.
Limitations: Information-extraction labels do not represent evidence stance or study-level scope compatibility.
Relevance to SCOPE: Potential resource for entity and relation/direction representation.
Possible research gap: Entity match alone cannot establish comparable populations, methods, or outcomes.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: Aspect-based Document Similarity for Research Papers
Authors: Malte Ostendorff; Terry Ruas; Till Blume; Bela Gipp; Georg Rehm
Research problem: Distinguish aspects under which research papers are similar instead of one coarse score.
Methodology: Pairwise multi-label document classification using citation section titles as aspect labels; compare Transformers and LSTM.
Dataset: 172,073 paper pairs from ACL Anthology and CORD-19.
Main findings: Reports SciBERT best with F1 up to 0.83 and qualitative evidence of finer-grained recommendations.
Limitations: Aspect similarity/recommendation is not support or contradiction; section title is a proxy label.
Relevance to SCOPE: Very relevant to faceted scholarly similarity and retrieval.
Possible research gap: Explicitly distinguish aspect similarity from evidence relation; test whether scope dimensions add value.
Verification status: Verified: ACL Anthology record and abstract; DOI resolves to canonical proceedings.

Full title: AVeriTeC: A Dataset for Real-world Claim Verification with Evidence from the Web
Authors: Michael Schlichtkrull; Zhijiang Guo; Andreas Vlachos
Venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36: Datasets and Benchmarks Track
Research problem: Verify real-world claims against time-appropriate open-web evidence with intermediate reasoning.
Methodology: Annotate question-answer pairs and textual justifications; provide a dataset, baseline, and evidence-aware evaluation scheme.
Dataset: AVeriTeC: 4,568 real-world claims fact-checked by 50 organizations.
Main findings: The paper reports verdict agreement κ=0.619 and introduces question-answer-based verification/evaluation.
Limitations: Web fact-checking is not scientific study comparison; the evidence source, temporal constraints, and verdict labels differ from selected-literature alignment.
Relevance to SCOPE: Strong adjacent prior art for evidence sufficiency, intermediate reasoning, and temporal leakage controls.
Possible research gap: Adapt evidence sufficiency and traceability lessons to scientific claims while comparing study scope; do not claim general claim verification novelty.
Verification status: Verified: NeurIPS proceedings record and DOI; authors, year, track, and paper abstract checked.
